answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly select a small set of staked agents for each task and penalize those whose independently checked results fail. Spawning a thousand accounts does not create a thousand free chances: each must tie up capital, and coordinated bad work risks losing it. The stake is an anchor, not proof of personhood; a walnut-sized deposit or velvet wording cannot substitute for enough capital to make attacks costly.
